The patient developed an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site, and was treated with antibiotics.
A swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, indicating a Staphylococcal infection.
The patient presented with fever and an elevated inflammatory syndrome, and blood cultures were obtained.

rationales.F03: Pacemaker implantation increases the risk of pacemaker pocket infection and device-related complications.
rationales.F06: The presence of an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site is highly suggestive of a pacemaker pocket infection or surgical site infection.
rationales.F10: The growth of Staphylococcus epidermidis from a swab of the lesion is highly suggestive of a staphylococcal infection.
rationales.F11: The negative blood cultures make septicemia less likely.
rationales.F12: The darkening and enlargement of the lesion despite antibiotic therapy suggests a worsening infection.
